Working notes:
- Option C (regional office) was rejected in all 10 observed requests, regardless of region, request type, size, submitter, or requester note. Avoid choosing C unless new evidence explicitly supports it.
- No outcomes are available for A (standard queue), B (priority desk), or D (external partner); their correct usage cannot yet be inferred.
- Do not assume the requester’s wording determines routing. Notes such as urgency, prior attempts, scanned paperwork, or regional-office submission did not make C valid.
- Ticket attributes observed: north/east regions; invoices, shipments, claims, and refunds; small/large requests. No confirmed routing rule linking these attributes to A, B, or D.

Working notes:
- Option C (regional office) was rejected in all 10 observed uses, across regions, request types, sizes, submitters, and requester notes. Avoid C unless new evidence supports it.
- Option A (standard queue) has mixed results. Accepted: north-region invoices and refunds (small invoice; small and large refunds). Rejected: shipments (north and south), claims (east; small and large), and an east-region invoice.
- Current evidence suggests A may be appropriate for north-region invoices/refunds, but this is not yet confirmed; size does not consistently determine validity.
- No outcomes are available for B (priority desk) or D (external partner); their usage cannot yet be inferred.
- Requester wording and submitter identity have not reliably determined routing. Urgency, repeated attempts, prior submissions, missing-document notes, and similar wording appeared in both accepted and rejected cases.
- Observed attributes include north, east, and south regions; invoices, shipments, claims, and refunds; small and large requests; and multiple submitting teams. No confirmed rule yet links these attributes to B or D.

Working notes:
- Option C (regional office) has been rejected in all 10 observed uses across regions, request types, sizes, submitters, and requester notes. Avoid C unless new evidence supports it.
- Option A (standard queue) is accepted for north-region invoices and refunds, including small and large refunds. New evidence confirms a small north-region refund via A. A was rejected for north/south shipments, east claims, and an east invoice. Size alone is not decisive.
- Option B (priority desk) is accepted for east-region claims (small and large), an east large refund, and a south large claim. It was rejected for an east large shipment and an east large invoice. B may fit claims particularly well, but the rule is not confirmed.
- Option D (external partner) is accepted for a south large shipment and an east small shipment. This suggests D may fit shipments, but evidence is limited and no D outcomes exist for invoices, claims, or refunds.
- Current tentative routing: A for north invoices/refunds; B for claims, especially east-region claims; D for shipments. Treat all as provisional because counterexamples and sparse coverage remain.
- Requester wording, urgency, repeated attempts, prior-submission language, missing-document notes, submitter identity, and size have not reliably determined routing.
- Observed regions: north, east, south. Request types: invoices, shipments, claims, refunds. No confirmed rule yet for every region/type combination.

Working notes:
- Option C (regional office) has been rejected in all 10 observed uses across regions, request types, sizes, submitters, and notes. Avoid C unless new evidence supports it.
- Option A (standard queue) is accepted for north-region invoices and refunds, including small and large refunds, and now for a large south-region invoice. It was rejected for a small south-region refund, plus north/south shipments, east claims, and an east invoice. Size alone is not decisive.
- Option B (priority desk) is accepted for east-region claims (small and large), an east large refund, a south large claim previously, and now a south small claim. However, it was rejected for a north small claim, an east small claim, and both small and large south claims in newer trials. Claim routing is not reliably B.
- Option D (external partner) is accepted for south large, east small, and north small shipments. This strengthens D as the tentative shipment choice, though coverage remains limited. No D outcomes exist for invoices, claims, or refunds.
- Tentative routing: A for north invoices/refunds and possibly south invoices; B only with supporting evidence, especially some east claims or selected south claims; D for shipments. Treat all as provisional because counterexamples and sparse coverage remain.
- Requester wording, urgency, repeated attempts, prior-submission language, missing-document notes, scanned paperwork, submitter identity, and size have not reliably determined routing.
- Observed regions: north, east, south. Request types: invoices, shipments, claims, refunds. No confirmed rule covers every region/type combination.

Working notes:
- Option C (regional office) has been rejected in all 10 observed uses across regions, request types, sizes, submitters, and notes. Avoid C unless new evidence supports it.
- Option A (standard queue) is supported for north invoices (small and large), north/south refunds in some cases, and south invoices (large). It failed for a small south claim and several north/south shipments, east claims, and an east invoice. Size and wording are not decisive.
- Option B (priority desk) is supported for an east large refund and some east/south claims, but has failed for both small east invoices, a north small claim, and multiple south claims. Do not assume B for claims or east requests merely from region/type.
- Option D (external partner) is now strongly supported for shipments: accepted for south small and large shipments and north small and large shipments. No confirmed D outcomes exist for invoices, claims, or refunds.
- Tentative routing: D for shipments; A for north invoices and likely south invoices; B only when supported by specific evidence (notably some east refunds or selected claims). East invoices remain unresolved; B is contradicted for small east invoices.
- Requester wording, urgency, repeated attempts, prior-submission language, missing-document notes, scanned paperwork, submitter identity, and size have not reliably determined routing.
- Observed regions: north, east, south. Request types: invoices, shipments, claims, refunds. Coverage remains sparse, with no confirmed rule for every region/type combination.

Working notes:
- Option C (regional office) has been rejected in all observed uses. Avoid C unless new evidence supports it.
- Option D (external partner) is not a general shipment rule. It was accepted for north small/large and south small shipments, but rejected for south large shipments and east small shipments (multiple cases). Shipment routing appears region/possibly size dependent; east shipments are unresolved/likely not D.
- Option A (standard queue) is supported for north invoices (small and large), south invoices (large), south small refunds, and north large refunds. It was rejected for a north large claim and has failed for several shipments, east claims, and an east invoice. A is plausible for invoices/refunds in north/south, but not guaranteed.
- Option B (priority desk) remains supported for an east large refund and some east/south claims, but failed for both small east invoices, a north small claim, and multiple south claims. Do not infer B solely from region or request type.
- No confirmed routing rule exists for every region/type combination. East invoices remain unresolved; B is contradicted for small east invoices. Claims remain especially inconsistent, including north large (A rejected) and north small (B rejected).
- Requester wording, urgency, repeated-attempt language, missing-document/scanned-paperwork notes, submitter identity, and size have not reliably determined routing.
- Tentative guidance: use A for supported north/south invoices and selected north/south refunds; use D only where shipment evidence matches (north shipments and south small shipments); use B only with specific supporting evidence, notably some east refunds or selected claims.
